# Exercise - Observational designs

These exercises cover the basic calculations for cross-sectional, cohort, and case-control studies.

## Exercise 1

A cross-sectional survey records obesity and arthritis status for 300 individuals:

```{r, eval=T,echo=T}
cross.tab <- matrix(c(36, 84,
                      24, 156),
                    nrow = 2,
                    byrow = TRUE,
                    dimnames = list(
                      Obesity = c("Yes", "No"),
                      Arthritis = c("Yes", "No")
                    ))

cross.tab
```

Compute:

1. the overall prevalence of arthritis;
2. the prevalence of arthritis among obese individuals;
3. the prevalence of arthritis among non-obese individuals.

Then explain why this study cannot establish the causal direction between obesity and arthritis.


```{r}
overall.prev <- sum(cross.tab[, "Yes"]) / sum(cross.tab)
prev.obese <- cross.tab["Yes", "Yes"] / sum(cross.tab["Yes", ])
prev.nonobese <- cross.tab["No", "Yes"] / sum(cross.tab["No", ])

overall.prev
prev.obese
prev.nonobese
```


## Exercise 2

A cohort study follows 200 individuals for a fixed period and gives the table below:

```{r, eval=T,echo=T}
cohort.tab <- matrix(c(40, 60,
                       10, 90),
                     nrow = 2,
                     byrow = TRUE,
                     dimnames = list(
                       Exposure = c("Yes", "No"),
                       Disease = c("Yes", "No")
                     ))
```

Compute:

1. the risk of disease in the exposed group;
2. the risk of disease in the unexposed group;
3. the relative risk.


```{r}
risk.exposed <- cohort.tab["Yes", "Yes"] / sum(cohort.tab["Yes", ])
risk.unexposed <- cohort.tab["No", "Yes"] / sum(cohort.tab["No", ])
rr <- risk.exposed / risk.unexposed

risk.exposed
risk.unexposed
rr
```

## Exercise 3

A case-control study on the same disease gives the following table:

```{r, eval=T,echo=T}
casecontrol.tab <- matrix(c(40, 20,
                            10, 30),
                          nrow = 2,
                          byrow = TRUE,
                          dimnames = list(
                            Exposure = c("Yes", "No"),
                            Disease = c("Yes", "No")
                          ))
```

Compute the odds ratio. Then explain why the relative risk cannot be interpreted in the usual way in a case-control study.


```{r}
or <-  (casecontrol.tab["Yes", "Yes"] * casecontrol.tab["No", "No"]) /
      (casecontrol.tab["Yes", "No"] * casecontrol.tab["No", "Yes"])
or
